name: Apollo 11
end_date: 1969-07-21 (ascent stage lunar liftoff; descent stage left on surface)
objective: Land astronauts on the Moon, perform surface exploration and return the crew safely to Earth.
outcome: Successful first crewed lunar landing; two astronauts landed, conducted surface activities and returned in the ascent stage to the command module.

related_equipment.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle
related_equipment.type: Crewed lunar module (descent stage remains on Moon; ascent stage returned to lunar orbit and was jettisoned)

name: Apollo 15
end_date: 1971-08-02 (rover operations ended with Apollo 15 surface activities)
objective: Allow astronauts to explore a wider area, transport scientific tools and samples, and extend the range of lunar surface traverses.
outcome: Successfully extended crew mobility during Apollo 15 surface EVAs; rover traveled 27.8 km across three traverses.

name: Surveyor 1
objective: Demonstrate a soft lunar landing and return surface images and basic information about the lunar surface.
outcome: Successful; first true soft landing on the Moon and demonstrated landing technology for later crewed missions.

name: Lunar Orbiter 1
objective: Photograph candidate Apollo and Surveyor landing sites and collect lunar environmental measurements.
outcome: Successful mapping mission; first U.S. spacecraft to orbit the Moon and captured the first image of Earth from the vicinity of the Moon.

name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
objective: Map the lunar surface and measure temperature, composition, radiation and illumination conditions to support science and future exploration.
outcome: Long-running active lunar mapping mission; supports landing-site selection, resource mapping and lunar science.

name: Viking 1
end_date: 1982-11-11 (Viking 1 mission page); Viking project overview gives Nov. 13, 1982
objective: Image surface and analyze soil and atmosphere, including biology experiments
outcome: Successful

name: Viking 2
objective: Study Martian surface, atmosphere and soil
outcome: Successful

name: Mars Pathfinder
objective: Demonstrate low-cost landing technology and deploy Sojourner
outcome: Successful

name: Mars Exploration Rover (MER-A)
objective: Study Martian rocks and soils for evidence of past water and assess the geological history of Gusev Crater.
outcome: Highly successful; exceeded its planned 90-sol mission and found strong evidence of ancient water-related environments.

name: Mars Exploration Rover (MER-B)
objective: Explore Martian rocks and soils for geological evidence of past water and assess whether ancient environments may have been habitable.
outcome: Highly successful; operated for nearly 15 years, found evidence of ancient water-altered environments, and traveled 45.16 km.

name: Mars Science Laboratory
objective: Assess whether Mars ever had environments capable of supporting microbial life
outcome: Successful

name: Mars 2020
objective: Search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect samples for possible return
outcome: Successful

name: Mars 2020 / Perseverance mission technology demonstration
objective: Demonstrate that powered, controlled flight is possible in Mars's thin atmosphere, then support rover route scouting and operations demonstrations.
outcome: Historic success: first powered, controlled flight on another planet; completed 72 flights, far exceeding the original five-flight plan.

name: Phoenix Mars Mission
agency: NASA / United States, with international partners
objective: Study the history of water and habitability in the Martian arctic by sampling soil and subsurface ice.
outcome: Successful planned surface science mission; confirmed water ice in the Martian subsurface and detected perchlorate.

name: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport (InSight)
agency: NASA / United States, with international partners
objective: Measure Mars's internal structure and activity using seismic, heat-flow and precision-tracking measurements.
outcome: Successful geophysical mission; measured marsquakes and improved understanding of Mars's interior.

name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
objective: Map elements and minerals and relay communications for surface missions
outcome: Successful

name: MRO
objective: Map surface, search for evidence of water and support communications
outcome: Successful

name: Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution
objective: Investigate how Mars lost much of its atmosphere
outcome: Successful

name: MESSENGER
launch_date: August 2004 (month precision for the card; see note)
objective: Study Mercury's geology, surface composition, magnetic field, and polar deposits.
outcome: NASA's MESSENGER was the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury. Its observations expanded knowledge of Mercury's surface composition, geological history, internal magnetic field, and polar deposits. The mission ended when the spacecraft impacted Mercury.

name: Magellan
objective: Map the surface of Venus using synthetic-aperture radar and study its gravity field.
outcome: Magellan mapped nearly all of Venus's surface with radar and revealed extensive volcanic terrain. The spacecraft's mission ended after a commanded plunge into Venus's atmosphere.

name: Galileo
objective: Study Jupiter, its major moons, and the surrounding magnetosphere.
outcome: Galileo orbited Jupiter and conducted close encounters with its major moons, while its atmospheric probe sampled Jupiter's atmosphere. The mission ended with a deliberate impact into Jupiter.

name: Cassini-Huygens
objective: Study Saturn, its rings, atmosphere, magnetosphere, and moons; the Huygens probe descended to Titan.
outcome: Cassini examined Saturn and its rings and moons for more than a decade. Its mission ended with a planned plunge into Saturn to help protect potentially habitable moons for future exploration.

name: Juno
objective: Investigate Jupiter's origin and evolution, interior, atmosphere, magnetosphere, and selected moons.
outcome: Juno studies Jupiter from a polar orbit and, in its extended mission, also observes aspects of the wider Jovian system and selected major moons.

name: Voyager 2
destination: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and interstellar space
objective: Explore the outer planets and continue measurements beyond the heliosphere.
outcome: Voyager 2 completed close flybys of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, then continued outward toward interstellar space. It is the only spacecraft to have flown by Uranus and Neptune.

name: New Horizons
objective: Explore the Pluto system and Kuiper Belt objects, and study the distant solar-system environment.
outcome: New Horizons made the first close exploration of Pluto and later flew past Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth. NASA reported in July 2026 that the spacecraft had awakened from a long hibernation and was preparing to transmit new science data.
